feedback:
Reviewed before this candidate has raced, so no result is stated for it. The evidence is the iteration 0 to 3 outcomes. Iteration 1 (kp 5.0, base 1.2, 5 sensors at +/-0.04 m) is the best raced design at 160.6. Iteration 2 showed that cutting base_speed to 1.0 did not reduce max_error (still 0.062 to 0.064 m) and lost the oval finishes (2 to 0). Iteration 3 showed that raising kp to 6.0 also left max_error at about 0.061 to 0.063 m and dropped the score to 123.3. Across all four iterations, line_loss_events stayed at about 1 per run and max_error stayed at the 0.06 m off-track limit whatever the speed or gain. Steering authority and speed are therefore not the binding limit, which supports the sensor-edge hypothesis.

The candidate is valid: 7 sensors within the x and y limits, weights within +/-2 and antisymmetric with the same sign convention as before, and line_loss unchanged. Its 0.02 m spacing with 12 mm footprints leaves no gap wider than the 25 mm tape, so the line is always seen. It reverts the controller to iteration 1's best setting, so this race isolates geometry against the 160.6 baseline. Note that the inner weights also change (0.67 and 0.33 instead of 0.5), so the race tests the array and its weights together; the outer weights remain at +/-1. Approval is for telemetry and a clean test of the edge hypothesis, not a performance claim.

What to change after the race, depending on what it shows:
- If line_loss_events falls toward 0 and max_error drops below about 0.055 m, the sensor edge was the cause. Keep the wider array, then raise base_speed in 0.1 steps (1.2 to 1.3) with kp 5.0 and kd 0.8 fixed, to recover completion time.
- If line_loss_events stays at about 1 per run with max_error near 0.06 m, the sensor edge is not the whole story. Test whether sensor_size 0.016 or a 0.04 m spacing (x = -0.06, -0.02, 0.02, 0.06 with 4 sensors, or similar) limits the signal, changing one of those fields only.
- If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.4 while max_error is below 0.05 m, reduce kd from 0.8 to about 0.5 with the wider array.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events falls toward 0 and max_error drops below about 0.055 m (iterations 1 to 3 all sat at 0.061 to 0.063 m): keep the 7-sensor array at +/-0.06 m and raise base_speed from 1.2 to 1.3 with kp 5.0 and kd 0.8 fixed. Reason: the drift is geometry-limited, so speed can be recovered for the time term.

If line_loss_events stays at about 1 per run with max_error near 0.06 m: keep the array and controller fixed, and change only sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016 (footprint 16 mm, still covering the 25 mm tape at 0.02 m spacing). Reason: iterations 0 to 3 showed one line loss per run whatever steering gain or speed was used, so the sensing footprint is the next candidate.

If steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.4 while max_error is below 0.05 m: lower kd from 0.8 to about 0.5 with kp 5.0 and the wider array. Reason: iteration 1 oscillation was 0.19 to 0.32 and iteration 0 with kd 0.3 gave 0.07 to 0.16, so kd can be trimmed if the wider array adds noise.
